annotation.authors_or_issuer: Weßel, M.; Ellerich-Groppe, N.; Schweda, M.
key_provisions_or_claims: Gender stereotypes in human-robot interaction may be used strategically to optimise eldercare outcomes.
Such stereotyping is increasingly problematic as older people's gender roles and preferences diversify.
Applies a principlist approach to map ethical problems and conflicts.
Discusses solutions toward culturally sustainable social robots in pluralistic societies.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper (Robophilosophy 2020) offering an explorative principlist ethical analysis of gender stereotyping in social robots for eldercare. It maps problems and conflicts and discusses possible solutions for culturally sustainable social robots in pluralistic late-modern societies.
annotation.title_clean: Stereotyping of Social Robots in Eldercare: An Explorative Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.title_en: Stereotyping of Social Robots in Eldercare: An Explorative Analysis of Ethical Problems and Possible Solutions
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335 (Robophilosophy 2020), IOS Press
